title: Zero parameter influence polynomial
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $B$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ whose constant-one element is indexed by $0$ and which is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product. For a positive integer $n$, any function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the stable influence polynomial at parameter zero equals the sum of the squares of the Fourier coefficients over precisely those multi-indices with exactly one nonzero coordinate and with that coordinate equal to $i$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite nonempty basis index set $\iota$ with decidable equality
A basis element indexed by $0$ is constant one
The basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
